title: Legacy FOL Comparison Fixture
description: Legacy hand-authored comparison fixture only. It is not a formal authority; upstream MMT source and generated IR are authoritative for imported declarations.

schema.reference_target: declaration id in any model collection

entity_types.name: Signature
entity_types.description: A vocabulary of sorts, function symbols, and predicate symbols with arities.

entity_types.name: Sort
entity_types.description: A domain kind used to type variables and function and predicate arguments.

entity_types.name: Variable
entity_types.description: A typed symbol that receives a value from a variable assignment.

entity_types.name: Term
entity_types.description: A variable or a function symbol applied to well-formed terms of matching sorts.

entity_types.name: Formula
entity_types.description: An inductively formed expression that is true or false relative to a structure and assignment.

entity_types.name: Structure
entity_types.description: A nonempty domain for each sort, with interpretations for signature symbols.

entity_types.name: Variable Assignment
entity_types.description: A sort-respecting mapping from variables to domain elements.

entity_types.name: Theory
entity_types.description: A set of sentences in a signature, considered together as assumptions.

relations.name: Function Symbol
relations.description: Signature declaration interpreted as a total function from argument domains to a result domain.

relations.name: Predicate Symbol
relations.description: Signature declaration interpreted as a relation on argument domains.

relations.name: Sentence
relations.description: A formula with no free variables.

constructors.name: Variable Term
constructors.description: A variable is a term of its declared sort.

constructors.name: Function Application
constructors.description: If f has input sorts s1…sn and result sort r, and ti has sort si, then f(t1,…,tn) has sort r.

constructors.name: Atomic Formula
constructors.description: P(t1,…,tn) is a formula when P has arity n and each argument term has its declared sort.

constructors.name: Negation
constructors.description: If φ is a formula, ¬φ is a formula.

constructors.name: Conjunction
constructors.description: If φ and ψ are formulas, (φ ∧ ψ) is a formula.

constructors.name: Disjunction
constructors.description: If φ and ψ are formulas, (φ ∨ ψ) is a formula.

constructors.name: Implication
constructors.description: If φ and ψ are formulas, (φ → ψ) is a formula.

constructors.name: Universal Quantification
constructors.description: If φ is a formula and x has sort s, ∀x:s φ is a formula.

constructors.name: Existential Quantification
constructors.description: If φ is a formula and x has sort s, ∃x:s φ is a formula.

judgments.name: Formation Judgment
judgments.description: Γ ⊢ t : s and Γ ⊢ φ : formula assert well-typed terms and well-formed formulas under signature context Γ.

judgments.name: Satisfaction Judgment
judgments.description: M, g ⊨ φ says formula φ is true in structure M under assignment g.

judgments.name: Semantic Consequence Judgment
judgments.description: T ⊨ φ means every structure satisfying all sentences of T also satisfies φ.

semantic_rules.name: Recursive Truth Conditions
semantic_rules.description: Variables read from assignments; functions and predicates read from structure interpretations; connectives use classical truth functions; quantifiers range over their sort domains.

satisfaction.name: Truth in a Model
satisfaction.description: Defined recursively: M,g ⊨ P(t̄) iff the interpreted tuple belongs to P^M; connectives follow classical clauses; M,g ⊨ ∀x:s φ iff every a in D_s satisfies φ under g[x↦a], and ∃ iff some a does.

theory.name: Theory
theory.description: A set T of sentences; M ⊨ T exactly when M satisfies every sentence in T.

semantic_consequence.name: Semantic Consequence
semantic_consequence.description: T ⊨ φ iff for every structure M, M ⊨ T implies M ⊨ φ. This is model-theoretic consequence, distinct from syntactic derivability.
